name: Pose a question for data collection
description: Student can pose a question of interest that can be answered by collecting data.
exampleOfSuccess: The student asks 'What is the most common way our class travels to school?'
commonError: Student poses a question that cannot be answered by collecting data.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to pose a question that could be answered by collecting data.

name: Collect categorical and numerical data
description: Student can collect data for a categorical variable and a discrete numerical variable.
exampleOfSuccess: The student records favourite sport (categorical) and number of pets (numerical).
commonError: Student records numerical data as categories, or mixes the two.
checkpointTask: Pose a survey with a categorical and a numerical question. Ask the student to collect the data.

name: Record data in a frequency table
description: Student can record collected data in a frequency table.
exampleOfSuccess: The student tallies responses and writes the totals in a frequency table.
commonError: Student leaves out categories with zero, or miscounts the tallies.
checkpointTask: Give collected data. Ask the student to organise it into a frequency table.

name: Use a digital tool or spreadsheet
description: Student can record data using a spreadsheet or digital data table.
exampleOfSuccess: The student enters survey results into a spreadsheet with category and count columns.
commonError: Student enters data in a disorganised way that cannot be read.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to record a small data set in a spreadsheet or digital table.

name: Create a column graph
description: Student can create a column graph from a data set with a scale.
exampleOfSuccess: The student draws a column graph of favourite fruits with labelled axes.
commonError: Student draws columns of uneven width or omits the scale or labels.
checkpointTask: Give a data set. Ask the student to draw a column graph with labels and a scale.

name: Create a picture graph with a key
description: Student can create a picture graph where one picture represents more than one item, using a key.
exampleOfSuccess: The student draws a picture graph where one symbol stands for 2 votes, with a key.
commonError: Student treats each symbol as one item, ignoring the key.
checkpointTask: Give a data set. Ask the student to make a picture graph with a key.

name: Read and interpret a graph
description: Student can read values from a graph and interpret them in context.
exampleOfSuccess: From a column graph, the student says soccer was the most popular sport.
commonError: Student reads the wrong value off the scale, or does not relate it to the context.
checkpointTask: Show a graph. Ask the student to read values and say what they mean.

name: Compare two representations of data
description: Student can compare two different representations of the same data and describe similarities and differences.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says the column graph and the table show the same totals, but the graph makes the most popular easier to see.
commonError: Student describes one representation without comparing.
checkpointTask: Show two representations of the same data. Ask the student to compare them.

name: Plan a statistical investigation
description: Student can plan a simple statistical investigation, including the question and how to collect data.
exampleOfSuccess: The student plans to survey the class about screen time and record it in a table.
commonError: Student starts collecting data with no plan or question.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to plan an investigation: the question, the data and how to collect it.

name: Carry out data collection
description: Student can carry out the data collection for their investigation.
exampleOfSuccess: The student surveys the class and records each response.
commonError: Student misses respondents or records responses inconsistently.
checkpointTask: Have the student carry out a planned data collection and record the results.

name: Represent the data
description: Student can represent the collected data in a suitable display.
exampleOfSuccess: The student makes a column graph of the survey results.
commonError: Student chooses a display that does not suit the data.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to represent their investigation data in a display.

name: Interpret and communicate findings
description: Student can interpret the results of an investigation and communicate them in terms of the question.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says 'most of the class has under 1 hour of screen time, which answers our question'.
commonError: Student reports counts without answering the original question.
checkpointTask: After the investigation, ask the student what the data shows about their question.
